subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin own RTS search, and what token, scope, and read-target contract should govern `assistant.search.context` calls?
rationale: This crosses Slack action-token handling, user/workspace search visibility, and OpenClaw's existing Slack read authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS search with ephemeral event-token handling, read-target checks or an explicit approved exception, redaction, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external plugin
options.body: Keep bundled Slack unchanged and require an external plugin or ClawHub path until maintainers want to own the RTS security boundary.

options.title: Reject workspace search for now
options.body: Leave Slack on conversation history/thread reads only and close future search PRs unless a maintainer sponsors the privacy and scope model.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS search with ephemeral event-token handling, read-target checks or an explicit approved exception, redaction, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent Slack assistant/action-surface history and already closed the broad action-parity PR by routing Slack search back to this issue.
